constraints: Run a real Native Bash job using async=true and a private gate/proof file. Preserve actual process/job/effect identity, original ToolResult and session owner. A sleep or callback counter alone is insufficient.

Consume the real Bash result through existing NativeWait where required. Current CliHooks aside_messages only handles edit/service/peer; automatic Bash aside consumption is not established by a comment. Do not create an async delivery framework just to satisfy the bank.

For hook evidence add only cfg(test-fixture) callback inside the existing CliHooks::after_tool_call_actual after its original checks/delegation, before it returns to Core. Keep native/value/args/result validation and original child-yield behavior intact. Avoid a new LoopHooks wrapper that silently drops required delegation.

The nonempty async callback must perform an actual write in the exact isolated cwd and block on its own private file gate. Record original call ID/session/cwd/resource and hook entry/exit. The real Core awaits this callback; no generic extension registry, public config or production callback is added.

Hold Bash and hook independently. Show actual Bash owner settled while hook remains held and the same Task has not captured, applied or removed its resource. Release hook, observe its proof file then original turn completion and same-resource capture. Do not merely hold a gate after the hook returned.
Exercise actual task cancel/abort while the original Bash is live and preserve its process/effect settlement or Unknown receipt. Dropping a release observer is not the task kill scenario.
Drop only the observer of the retained original release flight, then join the same flight; inspect durable started/settled effect IDs and physical cwd. Do not invoke an alternate finalizer.
This proves the actual Core async-hook/Host Task settlement contract under the declared fixture Host binding. It does not implement or accept the OMP extension product surface.
